alignments.note: Rule 9: the supplied subject rides with the finite verb, headed on the lexical verb.
Rule 65's English-side test: the ASV writes *also* for the intensifying καί.

Rule 102's contrast: the Greek is anarthrous, so no article competes and the supplied *psalm* is a rule 7 helper on the substantival adjective, which keeps the head under rule 17's generic-noun clause.
Rule 15 permits the discontinuity around the negative.

Rule 102: the article's complement is a substantival adjective with no expressed head noun, so the nominal the ASV supplies is the article's own and rule 17's generic-noun clause does not reach it, being scoped to anarthrous Greek. Rule 20's displacement empties only the determiner slot — σου takes *thy* — and rule 54's οἱ ἡμέτεροι -> *our people* keeps the supplied nominal on the article even so. Reading the article as wholly unrepresented and *One* as the adjective's own completion is the competing analysis.
Rule 20: the genitive pronoun takes the English possessive.

Rule 102 leaves the substantival adjective bare where an article stands to take the supplied nominal, as τὸν πτωχόν -> *the … man* and *poor* does, and as this chapter's τὰ ὅσια -> *the … blessings* and τοὺς πρώτους -> *the … men* do at ACT.13.34 and ACT.13.50.
Rule 61: the infinitival marker belongs to its own verb.

review_notes: Corrected τὸν ὅσιόν σου: the accepted reading left the article unrepresented under rule 20 and gave the whole *Holy One* to the adjective under rule 17. Rule 102 scopes rule 17's generic-noun clause to anarthrous Greek, and rule 54 says in terms that the article still recovers a supplied nominal where a possessive has taken the determiner slot. The article now takes *One* and the adjective a bare *Holy*, which is how ACT.13.34 and ACT.13.50 already read the same shape.
The verse's anarthrous ἑτέρῳ -> *another psalm* is unchanged and is rule 102's contrast standing in the same verse: there no article competes, so the adjective keeps the supplied noun and the head.
